findings.title: readSequence loops forever or misbehaves on indefinite length (-1)
findings.body: readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding. The loop `while (length > 0)` then skips parsing and returns an empty list. A sequence whose declared length exceeds the available data fails with an IOException from read(). The error handling is lenient or inconsistent on malformed input. Trailing bytes are not checked, and a truncated element is only caught indirectly.

findings.title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` build encoders and discard the results. They have no effect and should be removed.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns an unrelated JDK provider
findings.body: The method returns the provider of the default KeyStore type, which is a Sun provider and not BouncyCastle. Callers that use BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER (derived from this provider's name) would then request algorithms by that provider name. Many of those lookups, such as getKeyFactory, are unsupported here anyway, so this can fail confusingly.

findings.title: Abstract order() added to a public SPI breaks existing implementations
findings.body: Adding the abstract method `order()` breaks every third-party CryptoProvider implementation at compile time and load time (AbstractMethodError in detectProvider). It should be a default method, for example returning 100, to stay compatible.

findings.title: Providers with equal order are silently chosen arbitrarily
findings.body: The previous check that failed on multiple providers is gone. Two providers with the same order, such as default and elytron (both 200), are now resolved by classpath order, and the loser is logged only at debug level. A misconfigured classpath is no longer detected.
